passage: On Thursday evening Vandana opened the class group chat on Mummy's phone. Madhuri had written a mean line about her dress and other kids had added laughing faces. Vandana's cheeks burned and her thumbs shook. She typed an angry reply and then deleted it. She took a screenshot instead. It felt as though the whole class was staring at her. She went to the kitchen behind the family's kirana shop and showed Mummy, who read it twice. "This is not your fault," Mummy said. Next morning they showed the class teacher, who said they would talk to Madhuri and the class about the chat.

qa.q: What did Vandana do instead of sending her angry reply?
qa.a: She deleted it and took a screenshot instead.

qa.q: What was Vandana feeling as she read the message in the group chat?
qa.a: Hurt and exposed, as if the whole class were staring, and angry enough to type a reply before deleting it.

qa.q: What steps helped Vandana handle the message?
qa.a: She saved the proof, did not reply in anger and told Mummy and then the class teacher.

qa.q: How might Madhuri have seen the message she wrote?
qa.a: Perhaps as a joke to get laughs from others, without thinking how much it would hurt, though the passage does not say what Madhuri was thinking.

grounding: Illustrates a child hurt by a classmate's mean group-chat message who saves proof, does not reply in anger and tells adults.

passage:
Tuesday night
At six today Tanuja posted in our class group: "Ojas smells like a dustbin, nobody sit near Ojas tomorrow." Eleven people reacted. ELEVEN. It felt like everyone was staring at me through the phone.
I typed a long mean answer about her teeth. Then I deleted it. Papa always says never fight in the group.
I took screenshots instead, even though my hands were shaking, and showed Papa. He read it twice, then sat next to me on the bed. "This is not your fault, and you were right not to reply." He wrote to our class teacher tonight with the screenshots, and she has already answered that she will speak to the class tomorrow.
I still feel sick about going to school. But not alone.
Ojas

qa.q: How many people reacted to Tanuja's post?
How did Ojas feel after seeing the post?
qa.a: Ojas felt hurt and exposed, as if everyone was staring through the phone.

qa.q: Which choices helped Ojas, and why?
qa.a: Deleting the angry reply, saving screenshots and showing Papa, who wrote to the class teacher that night.

qa.q: How might Tanuja see her post compared with Ojas?
qa.a: Tanuja may think it is just a joke for laughs, while for Ojas it is public and deeply hurtful.

grounding: A child mocked in a class group chat feels hurt and exposed, saves proof instead of replying and tells a parent, who contacts the teacher.

passage:
The class group on Ma's phone buzzed during dinner in their small house near the Rewa bus stand. Hrithik had posted a voice note: someone copying Ankita reading English aloud, stretching every word, with the caption "Our Ankita, newsreader!" Laughing replies piled up underneath.
Ankita's face burned. She wanted to vanish under the charpai. She also wanted to send something nasty back.
Instead, she held the phone out. "Ma, listen."
Ma listened once, pressed her lips together, and helped Ankita save the voice note and the replies. Then she called the class teacher, who promised to remove the post that night and speak to Hrithik's parents. "It's not your fault, bitiya," Ma said, stroking her hair.

qa.q: What caption did Hrithik post with the voice note?
What was Ankita feeling when the voice note played?
qa.a: She felt humiliated and exposed; her face burned and she wanted to vanish.

qa.q: What did Ankita and her mother do instead of replying?
qa.a: They saved the voice note and the replies and called the class teacher that night.

qa.q: How might Hrithik see the post compared with Ankita?
qa.a: Hrithik may think it was a harmless joke, but for Ankita it was public and painful.

grounding: A girl mocked by a classmate in a group chat feels exposed, saves the proof instead of replying, and tells her mother, who contacts the teacher.
